thread:
morgan: Nightly eval alert: +5.7% regression on legal-clauses prompt set after last night's quant+batch change. Failures are concentrated on prefix-sensitive generations. Posting a couple of bad outputs below.

bench-bot: nightly-run: model=redwood-7b-q4_0 batch_policy=adaptive quant_profile=agg_v3 
summary: pass_rate=94.3% (was 100% yesterday), delta=-5.7% 
regressed_prompts=12/220; top failure class=incorrect clause enumeration
link: https://ci/internal/nightly/1865432

morgan: Example failing generation (expected enumerated items, model repeated item 2):
```
PROMPT: Draft a list of 4 standard termination clauses for service contracts.
GENERATED: 1) Termination for convenience
2) Termination for convenience
3) Termination for breach
4) Survival of obligations
```

anya: who rolled the quant+batch change? saw the deploy at ~02:10 UTC from gavin's PR?

ci-bot: deploy-bot: deploy completed 2026-06-15T02:09:58Z by gavin. changes: quant_profile=agg_v3, batch_window_ms=6 -> 4, prefix_kv_cache.compression=on

raj: quick hypothesis: prefix KV slot aliasing after shorthash truncation + tighter batch window. quantized kernels changed alignment so we might be evicting/merging different prefixes into same slot under load. That would cause non-deterministic prefix reuse.

kevin: can you paste the reproducer command? I want to run locally with deterministic seeds.

morgan: repro: run the nightly evaluator with these flags: 
```bash
./eval_runner --model redwood-7b-q4_0 --promptset legal-clauses --seed 42 --batch_window_ms 4 --enable_prefix_cache=true --repeats 3 --output=out.json
```
If I flip `--enable_prefix_cache=false` the failures disappear in 10/10 runs.

anya: interesting. so cache off => good. suggests collision rather than model quality.

raj: I pulled a memory dump from the failing run. notice these two short hashes mapping to same slot id: 
```
slot 0x3f -> shorthash 0x7a2b (tenant=acme)
slot 0x3f -> shorthash 0x7a2b (tenant=beta)
```
Given we use 16-bit shorthash by default, cross-tenant aliasing can happen under high slot pressure. Quantized kernel introduced smaller kv-frames so eviction timing changed.

morgan: ACK. Any quick mitigation besides full revert? We have customer-facing alerts.

kevin: short-term patch: increase shorthash to 24 bits and add per-tenant random salt when computing shorthash. Low-risk config change we can roll as a canary. Performance cost negligible.

eva: I can prototype the salt+bits change. Also add a TTL-based probe so we detect rapid aliasing spikes per model.

bench-bot: job queued: perf-smoke for shorthash=24 salt=true on canary pool (id: canary-3); URL: https://ci/internal/perf/1865433

anya: also add an integration test: run promptset with 10K short prefixes and assert deterministic outputs across 5 runs. Add that to nightly.

raj: long-term: move to tenant-scoped slot assignment (virtualized slots) so we avoid cross-tenant collisions entirely. But that's larger infra work.

morgan: agreed. Action items: 1) eva -> patch shorthash+salt and submit PR by EOD, 2) kevin -> prep hot canary rollout and rollback plan, 3) anya -> add deterministic integration test to nightly. I'll open the incident and notify CS.

ci-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1144 "prefix cache aliasing -> legal-clauses nightly regression" assigned to eng-ml. link: https://incident/INC-2026-1144

kevin: quick note: set `prefix_kv_cache.per_tenant_salt=true` in canary, monitor pass_rate and p50/p95 latency. If pass_rate recovers and latency delta <1%, promote.

eva: PR draft pushed: "kv: increase shorthash to 24 bits and add tenant salt" -> https://git/internal/pull/4821, tests: unit + memmap verify.

morgan: thx. @bench-bot can you re-run the nightly with canary patch once CI passes?

bench-bot: re-run queued: nightly with canary patch after PR merge. will post results.

anya: small follow-up: add a logging metric for dual-write collisions (count of slots observed with >1 active prefix) so ops can alert before evals.

raj: +1. I'll add a small diagnostic hook into the cache client; we can sample once per minute.

morgan: thanks team. we'll treat this as high-priority until pass_rate returns to baseline. :white_check_mark:

kevin: thumbs up :thumbsup: 

ci-bot: CI check passed for PR 4821 (unit+lint).

bench-bot: nightly canary finished: pass_rate=99.6%, delta vs yesterday=-0.4%. full logs: https://ci/internal/nightly/1865433/results

morgan: marking incident resolved pending monitoring retention. Closing thread for now.
